claims.body: The Penguins roll four lines, but the Sabres lean on their top six. Pittsburgh is one of the league’s best for depth, and Buffalo is one of the worst. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Penguins.

notes.text: Egor Chinakhov is on injured reserve and missed their last game.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 14 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 57% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 91:33 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Evgeni Malkin returned in their last game after missing 2 games.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Nick Robertson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 2% with his old team last season.
Zach Benson is out (upper-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Konsta Helenius is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 13 games.
Noah Östlund is on injured reserve, reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.

story.head: The Penguins need a win
paras: The Sabres have won two in a row, the last a 5-1 rout of the Rangers. The Penguins are on a five-game losing streak. Going in, the Pens are last in the Metropolitan (31st in the NHL) and the Sabres sixth in the Atlantic (19th).

The Penguins have played better than their record (.333) says: their chances are worth about .539, and their finishing has held them back. The Sabres’ record (.520) is about what their chances are worth. If the Penguins’ record were closer to their chances, like the Sabres’, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). On the other side, the Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd) and get their defensemen shooting (5th), but don’t block many shots (30th). The Penguins roll four lines, but the Sabres lean on their top six. On top of that, the Penguins could find some good looks against the Sabres, who give up plenty of them.

Evgeni Malkin (7 G / 13 A / 20 P in 20 GP) leads the Penguins in scoring, and Tommy Novak (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 24 GP) has a team-high nine goals. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (17 G / 13 A / 30 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Jack Quinn (14 G / 11 A / 25 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind.
Sergei Murashov (2-6-1 / .890 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to start for Pittsburgh, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (8-4-3 / .884 SV% in 14 GS) for Buffalo.
